questions.q: What two columns make up the drill hierarchy built on dw.DimTerritory for this page?
options: TerritoryAlternateKey and TerritoryKey
TerritoryGroup (region) above TerritoryName (individual territory)
CustomerType and TerritoryName
ProductName and CategoryName
questions.explain: TerritoryGroup sits above TerritoryName in the hierarchy, letting an Executive click from a region down into its individual territories.

questions.q: Why is [Pct of Company Total] added as a label on the territory bar chart, rather than just showing raw Total Sales dollars?
options: Raw dollars cannot be displayed as a data label in Power BI
It answers the harder question of whether a territory is proportionally strong, not just large because it belongs to a big region
Percentages are required by Power BI licensing for bar charts
It replaces the need for the drill hierarchy entirely
questions.explain: A bar of raw dollars shows which territory sold the most; the percentage label shows how much of the whole company total that represents.

questions.q: Why does [Pct of Company Total] need [Total Sales (All Territories)] specifically, rather than just [Total Sales], as its denominator?
options: Because [Total Sales] cannot be used inside a DIVIDE function
Because the denominator must stay a fixed, unfiltered company-wide total regardless of which bar or drill level is currently selected, which is exactly what the ALL-based measure provides
Because [Total Sales (All Territories)] is always larger by a fixed percentage
There's no real difference between the two measures
questions.explain: Every bar's percentage needs to be computed against the same constant, unfiltered denominator — which is what ALL(DimTerritory) inside Total Sales (All Territories) provides.

questions.q: Why does this page's drill hierarchy need to respect the same quarter/year slicer as the Executive Summary page?
options: Drilling into a territory without a shared time filter could mix multiple periods together instead of showing the selected quarter's numbers
Power BI requires all pages in a report to share identical slicers
It has no real effect on the numbers shown
Only to make the formatting look consistent
questions.explain: Without the slicer applying correctly, drilling into a territory could silently show an all-time total instead of the quarter currently selected — confirming this interaction is part of finishing the page correctly.

questions.q: What visual type is used for the drillable territory chart on this page?
options: A card visual
A clustered bar chart built on the TerritoryGroup → TerritoryName hierarchy
A single-value KPI tile with no hierarchy
A matrix with no drill capability
questions.explain: A clustered bar chart using the drill hierarchy lets an Executive click a region bar and expand into its individual territories live.
